thread:
Maria Chen: quick heads-up — we saw another p99 spike during the 18:00 load test. seems correlated with the batch-scaling change we pushed yesterday. can we do a fast triage? :eyes:

Kevin Patel: which change specifically? microbatch sizing or kernel selection?

Maria Chen: both, unfortunately. the autoscaler increased microbatch target from 8 -> 16 for GPUDuty pools. runtime then switched kernel strategy for small seqs which regresses tail. p95 is ok, p99 jumps ~120ms.

Sasha Ivanov: do you have profiling snippets? can we see which kernel got chosen and time breakdown (matmul, softmax, kv cache ops)?

Maria Chen: posting a short extract from perf profiler:
```
# hot path sample (avg of slow tail requests)
kernel: matmul_tiled_sm80_fp16 -> 35.4ms
kernel: matmul_warp_fp16_fallback -> 112.8ms  <-- chosen for batched shapes >8
kv_get: local cache hit -> 1.1ms
kv_get: remote miss (cold) -> 48.9ms  <-- cross-region fallback penalty
total (p99 sample) -> ~165ms
```

Oliver Wang: ugh. so two amplifying factors: 1) kernel selector picks slower kernel at larger microbatch sizes for our short-seq workload, 2) routing fallback to a different region kills KV cache warmness. combined results in long tails.

Kevin Patel: is kernel change deterministic given shape? i.e. batch_size x seq_len distribution changed and selection threshold crossed?

Maria Chen: yes. kernel selector uses heuristics + microbenchmark table. for batch >= 12 it prefers a 'wide' matmul kernel that has higher throughput for long-seq/large-mat shapes, but for short seq it's worse due to SM utilization patterns. we hit the threshold when autoscaler aggregated more requests.

Sasha Ivanov: do we have telemetry to show how often requests hit the cross-region fallback vs local region?

Maria Chen: infra events show ~2.8% of requests were rerouted because the primary pool was saturated and policy allowed cross-region burst. of the rerouted ones, kv cache miss rate was ~72% (we don't replicate KV across regions).

Oliver Wang: rough math: 2.8% * (cold remote penalty ~49ms) gives ~1.4ms added on average, but for p99 those remote misses concentrate in the tail and stack with slower kernel -> big jump.

Kevin Patel: actionable ideas: (A) lower microbatch cap to keep kernel selector in fast path (B) bump kernel selection score via microbench for our seq distribution (C) prefer routing sticky to same region for low-latency customers (D) replicate minimal KV state / prewarm on fallback target.

Maria Chen: agreed. I'm leaning for quick mitigation (A) + (C) while we do (B) and (D) medium-term. we can roll back batch cap in < 30m.

Sasha Ivanov: for (B) can we add a topology-aware microbenchmark run at startup that populates a per-node kernel preference table keyed by (seq_len_histogram, batch_threshold)? then selector consults that rather than one-size thresholds.

Oliver Wang: that sounds great. also for (C) we should tighten fallback policy: prefer intra-region capacity first, and when cross-region unavoidable, do N-second stickiness to let KV warm on target before routing more.

Kevin Patel: small experiment idea: run synthetic workload that mimics short seqs with bursty arrival. run with batch_cap 8 vs 16 and compare p95/p99 kernel breakdown. I'll spin this up in canary.

Maria Chen: thanks. canary plan: revert batch cap to 8 on canary pools, enable sticky intra-region routing on that canary, run 2h soak with bursty pattern, capture profiler + kv hit/miss, and then compare.

deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: revert-batch-cap -> eng-runtime-canary (3 nodes). scheduled in 5m.

infra-bot: note: cross-region burst routing currently controlled by policy `burst_fallback: region_priority=eu->us->ap`. changing stickiness may increase local queueing during high load. consider transient 429s vs p99 increase.

Maria Chen: good point. we'll watch 429 rate. prefer a small measured p99 improvement over system-wide 429s. we'll set a conservative sticky window (30s) and lower batch cap to 8.

Sasha Ivanov: follow-ups (assigned):
- Kevin: run canary perf comparison and post p95/p99 histograms + kernel selection tables (ETA 3h)
- Maria: update routing config on canary to add 30s stickiness + monitor 429s (ETA 30m)
- Oliver: prototype per-node kernel microbench script and add to onboarding (ETA next week)
- Infra: evaluate KV replica or async prewarm options (infra team to own)

Kevin Patel: I'll also capture tail traces for the slowest 0.1% to double-check there's no unrelated I/O stall.

Maria Chen: thanks team. will update this thread with canary results. :thumbsup:

Oliver Wang: ack.

Sasha Ivanov: ack.

Kevin Patel: starting canary run now. linking results in ~3h.

deploy-bot: canary revert-batch-cap deployed to eng-runtime-canary at 1769510200

Maria Chen: got initial telemetry: 10m in, p99 dropped from ~165ms -> ~92ms on canary. kv remote misses disappeared for sticky group. more detailed numbers when Kevin posts his run.

Kevin Patel: posted comparison summary: p95 similar, p99 improved 44-55% depending on region. kernel selection table confirms reverted batch kept fast matmul kernel. attaching perf gist: https://internal.gist/reports/176951

Maria Chen: great. next steps: ship batch cap change to prod with gradual rollout and schedule kernel microbench work. I'll open a release PR for the batch cap change and routing tweak.
__notes: This document follows agents.md schema for slack threads: single continuous string of messages prefixed by sender names. No title field present.
